prompt.context: Our client is a private equity firm experienced in the satellite industry (specifically communications and imagery) as well as government markets. They are considering an investment in I-Sight, a satellite imagery provider who supplies the imagery for applications such as Google Maps and the Intelligence Community's geospatial analysis.
prompt.question: Should our client proceed with the investment in I-Sight?

clarifying_info.a: The client is considering an investment horizon of 5-7 years in the U.S.

clarifying_info.q: Is I-Sight intended to be integrated with other portfolio companies?
clarifying_info.a: I-Sight is intended as a stand-alone entity; there is no planned fit with portfolio companies.
There are 4 main players in the market: I-Sight, Geo, Sat-Image, and Geo-Image.
I-Sight has a 40% share in the market.

clarifying_info.q: What is the market growth rate?
clarifying_info.a: The market has grown 10% over the last 3 years as GIS applications grow (consumers using Google Maps, growing agricultural and financial applications).

exhibits.title: Satellite Launches
exhibits.shows: A timeline showing satellite launch and expiration dates for all four competitors (I-Sight, Geo, Sat-Image, GeoImage), color-coded by competitor, spanning from T-16 to T+8 relative to today.
exhibits.data: I-Sight satellites: ISight-1 (launched and expires within timeline), ISight-2 (launch planned), ISight-3 (launch planned). Competitors also have multiple satellites with launch/expiry dates marked on the timeline.

exhibits.title: Satellite Payment Rates
exhibits.shows: A two-part table showing (1) payment rates per minute of satellite imagery by geographic region, and (2) time-of-day premium rates per minute.
exhibits.data: Americas: 40% of imagery, $125/min; Europe & Middle East: 10%, $100/min; Asia & Australia: 25%, $100/min; Africa: 20%, $75/min. Time premiums: 00:00-3:59 = 0%, 4:00-7:59 = 20%, 8:00-11:59 = 50%, 12:00-15:59 = 50%, 16:00-19:59 = 0%, 20:00-23:59 = 0%. Note: premiums are charged for higher visibility hours.

framework: (1) Market dynamics: market size & growth, competition, market share, trends, regulations
(2) Business situation: revenue streams & profitability, key differentiators, management effectiveness, pricing
(3) Transaction considerations: financing ability, fit with PE portfolio & strategy, investment horizon

questions.prompt: How would you analyze the market for satellite imagery? Who are the key customers and what are their demand drivers? What is the outlook for satellite imagery?
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment the market into two buckets: Government and Commercial. For government, identify the 5 key customers (NGA, DIA, CIA, FBI, DOD) and their fixed annual spending. For commercial, use Exhibits A and B to calculate total market size. Strong candidates recognize payments are in $/min and calculate minutes per year from satellite operating hours.

math.setup: Government market: 5 agencies x $50M annual spend. Commercial market: number of satellites x minutes per year x average rate per minute.
steps: Satellites in operation from Exhibit A: 4 imagery satellites currently in orbit (one per competitor)
Minutes per satellite per year = 1,440 min/day x 365 days = 525,600 min/year
Average base rate from Exhibit B (weighted by % imagery): (40% x $125) + (10% x $100) + (25% x $100) + (20% x $75) = $50 + $10 + $25 + $15 = $100/min
Time premium: higher-visibility hours (4:00-15:59) account for roughly 1/3 of the day at 20%-50% premium; blended premium ~20% on average, so effective rate = $100 x 1.20 = $120/min
Commercial total = 525,600 min/year x $120/min x 4 competitors = $252,288,000
math.answer: Total satellite imagery market ~$502M; Government ~$250M, Commercial ~$252M

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit A, what does I-Sight's satellite position tell you about its competitive situation and future prospects?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that I-Sight is in a strong competitive position: it plans to launch more satellites (ISight-2, ISight-3), which should be more efficient and precise. However, satellites not yet in orbit represent uncertainty and launch-delay risk that could immediately impact revenue projections.

recommendation: Recommend proceeding with the investment process in I-Sight
The market is growing (10% over last 3 years) with strong demand drivers from GIS, government, and commercial applications
I-Sight holds a strong 40% market share and planned new satellite launches could drive higher rates for more precise imagery
risks: Market risk: Government budgets are constrained due to increasing fiscal deficit; programs could be contracted
Market risk: Commercial customers have substitutes such as aerial imagery (images taken from airplanes)
Business risk: Many of I-Sight's satellites are not yet in orbit; any delays in the launch schedule would immediately impact revenue projections
next_steps: Customers: Analyze criticality of satellite imagery for government customers; evaluate substitute technologies such as aerial imagery
Market share: Anticipate competitive responses to I-Sight's planned launches; assess whether I-Sight can maintain 40% share and whether new satellites change payment rate dynamics
Launch schedule: Assess likelihood and historical frequency of satellite launch delays to stress-test revenue projections
